A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SceneCOT and SceneCOT-185K. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MSQA and Beacon3D evaluations, component ablations, oracle experiments, qualitative cases and dataset-quality audits.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds grounding evaluations, zero-shot QA results, latency measurements and internal recognition accuracy.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the four-stage procedure, LLaVA-1.5/PQ3D components, training losses, symbolic engine and two-expert inference routing. The additional evaluations do not establish a change to SceneCOT itself.

E1.justification: v3 adds SQA3D and ScanQA zero-shot QA and grounding evaluations, and directly evaluates Nr3D grounding rather than using Nr3D only as a data source. This substantially broadens evaluated task coverage within ScanNet; the existing training-data coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the matched QA and coherence tables is unchanged. However, the new zero-shot comparison evaluates a Chat-Scene variant trained on grounded QA to predict object IDs before answering (Appendix C.2), adding a substantive comparator adaptation.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce Top-1 and F1@50 grounding evaluations, zero-shot QA evaluated with EM-R, and latency and internal-stage accuracy measurements. Appendix C.3 also introduces an SQA3D-G annotation audit. The original MSQA/Beacon3D evaluation settings and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3 and D add focused annotation-quality, inference-cost and internal-recognition analyses, including stage-wise latency. The existing component ablations, oracle-grounding study and qualitative success/failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides seed-based aggregation, confidence intervals or significance testing. The added results continue point-estimate reporting; the new annotation audit and reproduction caveat do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial grounding, zero-shot QA and diagnostic results in Tables 4 and 11–14, including SceneCOT grounding F1@50 of 51.6 on SQA3D and 40.8 on ScanQA, and 10.4-second latency. Tables 1–3 retain their results. The appendix counting score changes from 47.9 in v1 Table 9 to 47.7 in v3 Table 10, although v3 Table 1 still reports 47.9.

T1.justification: The loss equation, coordinate constructions and Algorithm 1 are retained. No new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, propositions or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about grounded stepwise reasoning, the 185K-instance dataset and improved grounding–QA coherence. The new experiments support these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning zero-shot generalization and baseline weaknesses on QA-driven grounding. Appendix D argues that recognition errors are negligible and discusses the latency–interpretability tradeoff; Table 11 qualifies Chat-Scene results with reproduction difficulties. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and code/data availability statement, clarifies QA-only baseline supervision in Table 1, and documents grounded-QA comparator training and ScanQA-G/SQA3D-G annotation construction. Existing implementation listings, prompts and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Arnold, Perceive, Ground, Reason, and Act, and LEO-VL, including a brief discussion of LEO-VL's efficient scene representation. The broader positioning around grounded CoT for 3D reasoning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized introduction and related-work edits, adds evaluation/analysis subsections and reproducibility/ethics statements, and changes the publication header. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact; appendix sections are renumbered around the additions.

P2.justification: v3 adds a chart of the existing dataset mixture and five compact tables covering grounding, zero-shot evaluation, annotation quality, latency and recognition accuracy. Figure 2 and Table 3 are relocated, while existing diagrams, ablation plots and qualitative panels retain their content and visual design.

improvement.justification: The additional grounding and zero-shot evaluations strengthen empirical support, while latency and recognition diagnostics expose practical costs and error sources absent from v1. These are useful extensions to an already established method and evaluation. The authors' Chat-Scene reproduction caveat and the new 47.7 versus 47.9 counting inconsistency limit the gain, but the added evidence and disclosure provide a clear, bounded improvement.
